paper.title: JMarkov: An Integrated Framework for Markov Chain Modeling (TOMS 972)

field: applied probability (Markov chain and queueing model analysis)
stack: Java (TOMS 972.zip: Java/jMarkov with lib/jMarkov.jar, src/jmarkov, src/examples/jmarkov/Kanban.java, test/jmarkov/KanbanTest.java; third-party MTJ 1.0 and JUnit 4.13.2 from Maven Central, sha256 pinned in recipe.sh)

claim.text: The first entry of the average measures of performance of the Kanban model (examples.jmarkov.Kanban, default parameters), getMOPsAvg()[0], equals 0.7003166576899312 as in the shipped KanbanTest.testGetMOPsAvg; absolute tolerance 1e-4, fixed in the queue entry before any run. Deterministic steady-state solve.

attempt: Reproduced at the registered claim (tol_abs 1e-4). The authors' shipped jar and shipped test class ran as shipped: junit.textui.TestRunner jmarkov.KanbanTest gives OK (3 tests), including testGetMOPsAvg (all seven MOPs within 1e-4 of the shipped array). A harness (impl/PrintKanban.java, calls getMOPsAvg() with the default parameters and prints it) gives 0.7003166565882202 on both passes, a difference of 1.1e-9 from the registered value. The harness needed one sandbox change to compile: the JDK 17 javac could not read /etc/java-17-openjdk (its java.security is a symlink to it), so tools/sandbox.sh now binds that directory read-only (--ro-bind-try). The runs of the authors' code were not changed by it.

original_attempt.reason: the shipped jar and the shipped test class run as documented in Java/TEST.txt (junit TestRunner); the third-party jars are the dependencies the INSTALL lists (MTJ) and JUnit for the test runner, fetched and hash-pinned, not patches.
